summary.headline: The tertiary cascade fix CORRECTS the cascade-ion physics (0.766->0.931x, primary unchanged, energy conserved) but DESTROYS the chemistry (G-values 0.91x->0.40x). The dense gen3+ radicals over-recombine in the per-primary IRT.
summary.conclusion: The pre-fix chemistry agreement (0.91x) was a COMPENSATION OF ERRORS: too few radicals (no tertiary cascade) balancing the per-primary IRT. The cascade-ion count and the chemistry are coupled through radical density (same theme as E17 cross-primary). A correct model needs BOTH the tertiary cascade AND a chemistry that handles the true radical density (cross-primary IRT with correct geometry/diffusion) — not one without the other. NOT MERGED; production stays at v0.5.0 (the validated compensation). The branch preserves the working implementation for when the chemistry side is fixed.
